ambiguities: Only one thread email exists before the 2001-05-31 17:30 UTC cut (inbox/156, 15:44 UTC). It states the cut as 6,599 MMBtu and the SIQ reduction from 125,000 to 118,401. The numbers agree with each other (40,000 - 33,401 = 6,599; 125,000 - 6,599 = 118,401). No competing reading is available at this cut.

Superseded figure: inbox/156 (6,599 cut, SIQ 118,401) is replaced by inbox/160 (2001-05-31 19:50 UTC), which says the cut 'is now 4,856' after ANR revised its allocation, and that SIQ goes from 125,000 to 120,144. Rejected the 6,599/118,401 reading because it is explicitly revised.

Tense: inbox/160 says Peoples 'will reduce' SIQ by 4,856, while inbox/156 said 'reduced'. Someone could argue the earlier reduction to 118,401 had already been executed. Rejected: inbox/160 is the latest word for May 30 and states 120,144 as the resulting SIQ. Nothing later in the visible thread reverts it.

Corroboration: Cora Pendergrass (inbox/159) reports end-of-day Northern Border Will County cuts totalling 4,856 (R0255F 1,131 + T1061F 3,725). These are NB contracts, not ANR 104684, but the total matches inbox/160 and the arithmetic checks (40,000 - 35,144 = 4,856; 125,000 - 4,856 = 120,144).
Distractors: inbox/173 (June 3, 295 cut, SIQ 124,705) and inbox/186 (June 5, 423 cut, SIQ 44,577) are for other gas days and do not apply to May 30.

Christian's conflict email (11440, 2001-06-05 11:07 UTC) comes after the 10:00 UTC cut. It is not visible and does not affect this answer.
June 7, 2001 is a Thursday, which matches the subject line and the emails.
The Thursday June 7 15:30 slot (11429/11430) was cancelled when Christian reported a fixed conflict (11440). Rejected that reading because it was replaced.

Christian offered 'earlier' on Thursday or Friday. No earlier Thursday time was ever proposed. Holly proposed 3:00 pm Friday (11444), Sara offered 3 pm Houston / 1 pm Portland Friday (11456), Christian said 'Good.' (11459), Sara asked Holly to schedule it (11461), Holly confirmed 'it's on Mark's calendar (3:00 pm - Friday, June 8)' (11465), and Sara confirmed 1 pm Portland Friday to Christian (11467). Subject-line trap: most emails keep the subject 'for Thursday, June 7' even after the move. The subject was dropped only in 11465/11467. The subject should not be read as the meeting date.

Nothing after 11467 (2001-06-06 09:30 UTC) and before the 2001-06-07 14:00 UTC cut changes the time.
